drsNoRecentDrill.^description: {$COUNT} region(s) have AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery source servers, protected for more than 90 days, with no successful recovery drill launched in the last 90 days. Replication alone does not prove that a server can be recovered: launch templates, networking, licensing, boot conversion and application start-up only get exercised when a drill instance is launched. Run non-disruptive drills regularly and after significant changes, then terminate the drill instances.
drsNoRecentDrill.shortDesc: Run DRS recovery drills at least every 90 days
ref: [REL13-BP03 Test disaster recovery implementation to validate the implementation]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/reliability-pillar/rel_planning_for_recovery_dr_tested.html>

drsReplicationUnhealthy.^description: {$COUNT} AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery source server(s) are not replicating healthily: replication is stalled, paused, stopped or disconnected, reports a replication error, or lags by more than one hour. While replication is unhealthy the latest recovery point ages, so a recovery would lose more data than the intended RPO, or may not be possible at all. Resolve the replication error shown for the server.
drsReplicationUnhealthy.shortDesc: Keep DRS source server replication healthy
